question: Did the retained flash-report sequence occur under one homogeneous human observation opportunity, or did attention and viewing conditions change after the first report?
baseline: Treat the nearly hour-long eclipse as one clock-time denominator and describe viewing limitations qualitatively.
treatment: Bind exact transcript transitions and later crew reflections into a time-ordered observation-state ledger, then test whether a homogeneous human-exposure denominator remains supportable.
oracle: Pass only when exact source identities, all timeline anchors, required ordering, frozen intervals, and later crew context reproduce while every causal, physical-event, calibrated-rate, and pixel claim remains withheld.
authority: Private deterministic transcript audit. It may classify the observation process as time-varying, but it may not estimate detection probability, physical event rate, completeness, causation, or clustering.
